exposure: mean arterial pressure (MAP) >=105 mmHg at 18-20 weeks
mean arterial pressure (MAP) >=105 mmHg at 24-28 weeks
cohort: The study included 300 pregnant women diagnosed with chronic hypertension.
finding: The incidence of superimposed preeclampsia was 43.3% among pregnant women with chronic hypertension, and high MAP >=105 mmHg during the late second trimester was identified as an important predictor associated with increased adverse neonatal outcomes.
